chunks: My Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about the two of them. He said: They are from the sunnah (prophetic tradition); so if you forget them, there is no repetition required of you.
And with this isnad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Miskan, from Malik ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about one who performed wudu (ablution) and forgot rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose, then remembered after he had entered into his salat (prayer). He said: There is no harm.
And with this isnad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
Rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose are not from wudu (ablution).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The meaning of his statement عليه السلام, “They are not from wudu (ablution),” is that they are not among the obligatory duties of wudu, even though they are among its sunnahs. The first report that we narrated from Sama'ah indicates this, and what also confirms that is the following:

My Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the two of them, and he said: They are from wudu (ablution), but if you forget them, then do not repeat.
As for what Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose are neither an obligation nor a sunnah; rather, what is upon you is to wash what is outwardly visible of the face. The meaning of this report is that they are not from the sunnah that it is impermissible to leave; as for their performance being an innovation, it does not indicate that.

What the Shaykh narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
Rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose are among what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم established as sunnah (prophetic tradition).

key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: the recommended prophetic practice, as distinct from an obligatory duty
key_terms.الِاسْتِنْشَاقُ: drawing water into the nose during wudu (ablution)
key_terms.فَرَائِضِ: obligatory duties whose omission affects validity

ai.seo_question: Are al-madmadah and al-istinshaq obligatory in wudu according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: These reports discuss whether rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose are part of wudu (ablution). The narrations and the compiler’s reconciliation indicate that they are from the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of wudu, not from its obligatory acts, so forgetting them does not require repetition of the wudu or the salat (prayer).
